answer: Make admission an insurance decision. Each identity must buy a fraud policy from an independent underwriter who pays the network if that identity is later proven to be a clone; the underwriter keeps the premium and eats the loss, so it screens applicants. Correlated applicants - same funding, same timing - are refused or quoted as one risk pool, and the first refusal ripples through the market. A farm of a thousand clones cannot buy a thousand cheap policies: the rest are priced at the summit of the curve. A jade seal records who carried each risk, and the karst of past claims stays public.
